additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) is characterized by a combination of mood episodes meeting criteria for mania or mixed episodes, together with psychotic symptoms such as delusions or hallucinations that also occur outside of mood episodes. To diagnose it, there must be a period of at least two weeks of psychosis without prominent mood symptoms, along with mood episodes present for a substantial portion of the illness. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with functional impairment that can range from moderate to severe, and it can be difficult to distinguish from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia unless the temporal relationship between mood and psychosis is carefully documented. Treatment typically involves mood stabilizers and antipsychotic medications, sometimes with adjunctive psychosocial interventions to address social and occupational dysfunction.

patient.stressor: About a year and five months ago, Andres and his wife moved from their longtime house in Las Piedras into a smaller apartment closer to their adult daughter after he had a minor fall, a change that disrupted his familiar routines of tending his garden, walking the same streets, and organizing neighborhood repair projects. Although he stayed involved with church and the senior center, he felt disoriented by the new environment and increasingly withdrew from leading community events, spending more time alone in his room with the radio. Over the following months, his family noticed that he became markedly less engaged in cooking, music rehearsals, and domino games, and that he seemed oddly flat and indifferent to traditions he once cherished, even as he occasionally mentioned experiences and beliefs that did not match what others observed. When he started skipping mass and choir, stopped caring for his plants, and his daughter realized he could no longer reliably manage simple household tasks or social commitments, she arranged for a home visit from his primary doctor, who then referred him for specialized psychiatric assessment.
patient.chief_complaint: “I just don’t feel like doing anything anymore—not cooking, not music, not even playing dominoes with my friends.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Lately I keep thinking the people in this new building and even some folks at church are part of a plan to watch me and see if I’m still fit to live on my own, like there are little tests hidden in everyday things, and no matter what my daughter says I can’t shake the feeling it’s all arranged around me.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m alone in my room with the radio off, I still hear a man’s voice clear as day calling my name and commenting on what I’m doing, sometimes telling me I’m failing my ‘mission,’ even though nobody else hears it and it’s not coming from outside.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: My daughter says I’ll just stand in the hallway for a long time holding a dish or the broom, not moving or answering her, or I’ll suddenly start pacing back and forth and waving my hands while I talk to myself about things that don’t match what’s going on around me.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Most days now I just sit on the edge of the bed staring at the floor, not picking up my guitar, not cooking, not calling anybody, and even when my grandson begs me to play dominoes or go to mass I feel like there’s no spark inside to get up and join in, like it all means nothing to me anymore.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Some weeks I’ll wake up feeling like a motor that won’t turn off, joking too loud and talking nonstop, and then in the same afternoon I can flip and start snapping at my wife and daughter over little things like how they fold the towels, getting so irritated that I surprise even myself.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: On those ‘high’ days I can’t sit still—I’m cleaning every corner of the apartment, rearranging the closets at midnight, planning big repairs for a building that isn’t even mine, starting ten things at once and not finishing any, like my body is being pushed from behind.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: There are times I feel sure God kept me alive from that fall because I’m some kind of special messenger for the neighborhood and that I could run the whole church better than the priest if they would just listen to my ideas, even though I can barely manage my own pills some days.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: Many nights I’ll sleep only two or three hours and still feel wired, sitting by the window till dawn making lists and plans in my head and telling my wife I don’t need sleep anymore because my mind is too busy with important things.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My thoughts race so fast that while I’m praying the rosary I jump from the Hail Mary to fixing the pipes, then to starting a new choir, then to worrying about spies in the hallway, all in a few seconds, and I can’t slow it down enough to finish a single idea.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: If I sit to read the Bible or watch a ball game, any little sound—the elevator ding, a car horn, a bird on the balcony—pulls me away so completely that I get up to check it, then notice the curtains, then start fiddling with the plants, and I forget what I was doing in the first place.

add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms and manic_episode occ: On my ‘high’ days when I’m buzzing around cleaning and talking nonstop, that same voice still calls my name and tells me I’m failing my mission, and I’m sure the neighbors are watching to see if I mess up.
add_requirements.manic_episode is present for the majorit: Ever since we moved to this apartment, those revved-up spells where I barely sleep, feel full of big plans, and can’t sit still have kept coming back and lasting longer than the quieter stretches in between.
add_requirements.delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2: There were a couple of long stretches this past year when I didn’t feel especially up or down, just flat and tired, but I still heard that man’s voice commenting on me and stayed convinced the people in the building were secretly testing me.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: These problems have gotten so bad that my daughter had to take over my pills and bills, I’ve stopped going to mass and the senior center, and I can’t be trusted to handle simple chores without getting stuck or confused.
add_requirements.duration: All of this really started to build up after we left our old house in Las Piedras and moved here about a year and a half ago, and it hasn’t settled back to how I used to be since then.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: For most of this past year, especially these last several months, I’ve been hearing that voice and feeling watched in this building even when my mood isn’t especially high or low.
add_requirements.manic_episode_duration: Not long after the move, I began having these long spells of feeling overcharged, sleeping very little, and rushing from one project to another, and that pattern has kept coming back over much of this past year.
